# Introduction and hypotheses

Insulin resistance in skeletal muscle precedes type 2 diabetes (T2D), and aging is itself a
major risk factor for both. Jin et al. (2011) profiled vastus lateralis biopsies from
normoglycemic people with or without a family history (FH) of T2D and from people with T2D,
and reported that increased serum response factor (SRF) activity marks insulin resistance.
The Hallmarks of Aging (López-Otín et al., 2013) predicts that age-associated changes should
involve mitochondrial dysfunction, deregulated nutrient sensing, altered intercellular
communication (inflammation), and loss of proteostasis.

Hypotheses tested here:

* **H1.** Unsupervised clustering of muscle transcriptomes separates samples by a biological
  factor (sex, diabetes status, or age), not at random.
* **H2.** Sex is the strongest single source of transcriptome-wide variation, driven by
  sex-chromosome genes.
* **H3.** A set of genes is correlated with age, and these genes are enriched for
  Hallmark-of-Aging processes (mitochondria / oxidative phosphorylation, extracellular matrix,
  inflammation).
* **H4.** Because the diabetic group is older than the other groups, part of any apparent "age
  signature" is confounded by diabetes; this must be tested explicitly.

# Data and preprocessing

* **Expression:** the course-provided `BE700_human_expression_1.csv` for GSE25462.
  The assignment explicitly states that this matrix is already log-normalized; no second
  log transform or additional normalization is applied here.
* **Phenotypes:** `BE700_human_pheno_1.csv`, containing the GEO sample metadata and
  the phenotype columns ending in `:ch1`.
* **Provenance boundary:** the metadata identifies GPL570 (Human Genome U133 Plus 2.0)
  and records GCOS v1.3/MAS5.0 processing with a trimmed-mean scaling target of 1500.
  This upstream processing is distinct from the log-transformed, annotated course matrix.
  The exact probe-to-feature aggregation script and annotation version were not supplied.
  The paper's main text describes U133A 2.0 and groups of 15/26/11 people, whereas GEO and
  the supplied matrix contain 15/25/10. This analysis uses the 50 supplied samples and their
  GPL570 metadata, not the paper's larger demographic totals.
* **Unit of analysis:** rows are gene-annotated expression features. Entries such as
  `A///B` have ambiguous multi-gene annotations; splitting them for annotation does not
  establish that the expression of A and B was measured independently.

```{r load}
expr_raw <- read.csv("data/BE700_human_expression_1.csv", check.names = FALSE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
genes <- expr_raw[[1]]
keep  <- !is.na(genes) & genes != ""
expr  <- as.matrix(expr_raw[keep, -1]); rownames(expr) <- genes[keep]

ph_raw <- read.csv("data/BE700_human_pheno_1.csv", check.names = FALSE,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))   # "missing value" -> NA
ph <- data.frame(
  sample   = ph_raw$geo_accession,
  title    = ph_raw$title,
  sex      = factor(ph_raw[["gender:ch1"]]),
  age      = num(ph_raw[["age (years):ch1"]]),
  bmi      = num(ph_raw[["body mass index (kg/m2):ch1"]]),
  whr      = num(ph_raw[["waist hip ratio:ch1"]]),
  hba1c    = num(ph_raw[["hemoglobin a1c:ch1"]]),
  fglu     = num(ph_raw[["fasting glucose (iv0gavg):ch1"]]),
  finsulin = num(ph_raw[["fasting insulin (iv0inavg):ch1"]]),
  si       = num(ph_raw[["si:ch1"]]),
  glu2h    = num(ph_raw[["2 hour glucose (ogtt):ch1"]]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ph$group <- factor(sub("^Muscle-", "", sub("-[0-9]+$", "", ph$title)),
                   levels = c("FamilyHistoryNegative", "FamilyHistoryPositive", "Diabetes"),
                   labels = c("FH-", "FH+", "T2D"))
ph$label    <- paste0(c("FH-" = "N", "FH+" = "P", "T2D" = "D")[as.character(ph$group)],
                      sub(".*-", "", ph$title))      # short plot labels, e.g. D3, N12
ph$diabetes <- factor(ph$group == "T2D", labels = c("No", "Yes"))
rownames(ph) <- ph$sample

stopifnot(identical(colnames(expr), ph$sample),
          !anyDuplicated(ph$sample), !anyDuplicated(rownames(expr)),
          is.numeric(expr), all(is.finite(expr)),
          all(apply(expr, 1, var) > 0),
          !anyNA(ph[, c("age", "sex", "group", "diabetes")]))
n_multimapping <- sum(grepl("///", rownames(expr), fixed = TRUE))
dim(expr)
```

The matrix has **`r nrow(expr)` expression features x `r ncol(expr)` samples** after
removing `r sum(!keep)` row with an empty annotation. Sample order matches the phenotype
table; expression values are finite and row identifiers are unique. Of the retained rows,
`r n_multimapping` contain `///` multi-gene annotations. Gene names below refer to these
annotations, with this measurement ambiguity retained.

```{r pheno-table}
summary_vars <- c("age", "bmi", "hba1c", "si")
cohort_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(ph$group), function(g) {
  rows <- ph$group == g
  out <- data.frame(group = g, n = sum(rows),
                    female = sum(ph$sex[rows] == "female"))
  for (v in summary_vars) {
    x <- ph[[v]][rows]
    out[[paste0(v, "_n")]] <- sum(!is.na(x))
    out[[paste0(v, "_mean")]] <- if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else
      mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  out
}))
cohort_display <- cohort_summary[, c("group", "n", "female")]
for (v in summary_vars) {
  cohort_display[[v]] <- sprintf("%.1f (n=%d)",
    cohort_summary[[paste0(v, "_mean")]], cohort_summary[[paste0(v, "_n")]])
}
knitr::kable(cohort_display, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Cohort summary: mean and available n for each measure; SI = insulin sensitivity.")
write.csv(cohort_summary, "results/cohort_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
kruskal.test(age ~ group, data = ph)
colSums(is.na(ph[, c("whr", "si", "glu2h")]))
```

**Data issues found.** (i) The T2D group is older than the FH- and FH+ groups, so age and
diabetes are associated in this sample and can confound expression comparisons (H4).
(ii) OGTT values are missing for all T2D subjects, SI for two, and waist-hip ratio for one.
The T2D SI mean uses its eight observed values; missing values do not erase the group mean.
(iii) One FH- subject has BMI 20 but WHR 1.36, an unusual combination requiring source
verification. It is not sufficient evidence of an entry error; WHR is not used for inference.

## Quality control

```{r qc-box, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="Per-sample distributions of the course-provided log-normalized matrix; no additional normalization was applied."}
ord <- order(ph$group)
boxplot(expr[, ord], outline = FALSE, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.5, names = ph$label[ord],
        col = c("grey85", "lightblue", "salmon")[ph$group[ord]], ylab = "log expression")
legend("topright", fill = c("grey85", "lightblue", "salmon"), legend = levels(ph$group),
       cex = 0.7, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n")
```

```{r qc-sex, fig.height=3.4, fig.width=4.5, out.width="55%", fig.cap="Sex check: XIST (X-inactivation) versus RPS4Y1 (Y-linked)."}
sexchk <- data.frame(XIST = expr["XIST", ], RPS4Y1 = expr["RPS4Y1", ], sex = ph$sex)
ggplot(sexchk, aes(XIST, RPS4Y1, colour = sex)) + geom_point(size = 2)
pred_sex <- ifelse(sexchk$XIST > 11 & sexchk$RPS4Y1 < 12, "female",
             ifelse(sexchk$XIST < 11 & sexchk$RPS4Y1 > 12, "male", "ambiguous"))
mm <- pred_sex != as.character(ph$sex)
knitr::kable(data.frame(sample = ph$label, reported = ph$sex, XIST = sexchk$XIST,
                        RPS4Y1 = sexchk$RPS4Y1, expression_says = pred_sex)[mm, ],
             digits = 1, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Samples whose expression disagrees with reported sex.")
```

The exploratory XIST/RPS4Y1 thresholds flag `r sum(mm)` of `r nrow(ph)` samples:
`r paste(ph$label[mm], collapse = ", ")`. These are expression--metadata discrepancies,
not diagnoses of sample mislabeling, contamination, or a karyotype. The two markers and
heuristic cutoffs are insufficient to determine the cause. Reported labels and all samples
are retained in the main analysis; flagged samples are excluded only in explicitly labeled
age and PCA sensitivity analyses. Multiple sex-chromosome markers and source records would
be needed before relabeling or permanently excluding a sample.

## Outlier samples

```{r qc-outlier, fig.height=3, fig.cap="Median Pearson correlation of each sample with all other samples. Red: below Q1 - 1.5 IQR."}
cc <- cor(expr)
diag(cc) <- NA_real_  # exclude self-correlation explicitly
medcor <- apply(cc, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
thr <- quantile(medcor, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR(medcor)
outl <- ph$label[medcor < thr]
o2 <- order(medcor)
barplot(medcor[o2], names.arg = ph$label[o2], las = 2, cex.names = 0.5,
        col = ifelse(medcor[o2] < thr, "firebrick", "grey70"), ylim = c(0.75, 0.9), xpd = FALSE,
        ylab = "median r with other samples")
abline(h = thr, lty = 2)
excl <- ph$sample[medcor < thr | mm]   # outliers + sex-discordant samples
```

The median between-sample correlation is `r round(median(medcor), 3)`.
Lower-correlation flags: `r if (length(outl)) paste(outl, collapse = ", ") else "none"`.
This within-dataset diagnostic does not establish technical failure or justify a numerical
comparison with RNA-seq datasets processed on other scales. The union of correlation and
sex-marker flags is `r paste(ph$label[ph$sample %in% excl], collapse = ", ")`.

# Heatmap of the muscle transcriptome

Genes were ranked by variance across samples and the 1,000 most variable were kept; each gene
was z-scored across samples. Samples and genes were clustered hierarchically (Euclidean
distance, Ward.D2 linkage).

```{r hm-prep}
v     <- apply(expr, 1, var)
top   <- names(sort(v, decreasing = TRUE))[1:1000]
z     <- t(scale(t(expr[top, ])))
ann   <- data.frame(Sex = ph$sex, Group = ph$group, Age = ph$age, BMI = ph$bmi,
                    row.names = ph$sample)
ann_col <- list(Sex = c(female = "#E7298A", male = "#1B9E77"),
                Group = c("FH-" = "grey70", "FH+" = "#7570B3", "T2D" = "#D95F02"))
```

```{r hm-all, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Top 1,000 most variable genes, z-scored, Ward.D2 clustering."}
pheatmap(z, show_rownames = FALSE, labels_col = ph$label, fontsize_col = 6,
         annotation_col = ann, annotation_colors = ann_col,
         clustering_method = "ward.D2", treeheight_row = 0,
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(100))
```

To see what lies under the sex signal, sex-associated genes were identified with a Welch
t-test (BH q < 0.05 and |mean difference| > 1 log unit) and removed, and the heatmap was redrawn
on the 1,000 most variable remaining genes.

```{r sex-genes}
tt <- apply(expr, 1, function(g) t.test(g ~ ph$sex)$p.value)
dm <- rowMeans(expr[, ph$sex == "male"]) - rowMeans(expr[, ph$sex == "female"])
sex_genes <- names(which(p.adjust(tt, "BH") < 0.05 & abs(dm) > 1))
length(sex_genes); head(sort(sex_genes), 25)
sex_variance_fraction <- sum(apply(expr[sex_genes, , drop = FALSE], 1, var)) /
  sum(apply(expr, 1, var))
expr_ns <- expr[setdiff(rownames(expr), sex_genes), ]
top_ns  <- names(sort(apply(expr_ns, 1, var), decreasing = TRUE))[1:1000]
z_ns    <- t(scale(t(expr_ns[top_ns, ])))
```

```{r hm-nosex, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Top 1,000 most variable genes after removing sex-associated genes."}
pheatmap(z_ns, show_rownames = FALSE, labels_col = ph$label, fontsize_col = 6,
         annotation_col = ann, annotation_colors = ann_col,
         clustering_method = "ward.D2", treeheight_row = 0,
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(100))
```

# Clustering patients

Both k-means (25 random starts) and hierarchical clustering (Ward.D2) were applied to the
samples, on the z-scored top-1,000 features with and without sex-associated features. The
number of clusters was chosen by average silhouette width for k = 2 to 6; a final k-means fit
at the selected k uses 25 random starts. Final-fit silhouette widths are reported separately
from the candidate-k fits. Agreement between methods is measured with the adjusted Rand
index (ARI). A best k among 2--6 does not itself establish discrete biological subgroups.

```{r cluster}
set.seed(700)  # isolate clustering from earlier plotting/interactive RNG state
ari <- function(a, b) {                       # adjusted Rand index
  tab <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tab); c2 <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  e <- c2(rowSums(tab)) * c2(colSums(tab)) / choose(n, 2)
  (c2(tab) - e) / ((c2(rowSums(tab)) + c2(colSums(tab))) / 2 - e)
}
run_clusters <- function(zmat) {
  X  <- t(zmat); d <- dist(X); hc <- hclust(d, "ward.D2")
  sil <- sapply(2:6, function(k) {
    km <- kmeans(X, k, nstart = 25)
    c(kmeans = mean(silhouette(km$cluster, d)[, 3]),
      hclust = mean(silhouette(cutree(hc, k), d)[, 3]))
  })
  colnames(sil) <- paste0("k=", 2:6)
  list(X = X, d = d, hc = hc, sil = sil)
}
cl_all <- run_clusters(z); cl_ns <- run_clusters(z_ns)
round(cl_all$sil, 3); round(cl_ns$sil, 3)
```

```{r cluster-assign}
k_all <- which.max(cl_all$sil["kmeans", ]) + 1
k_ns  <- which.max(cl_ns$sil["kmeans", ]) + 1
ph$km_all <- factor(kmeans(cl_all$X, k_all, nstart = 25)$cluster)
ph$hc_all <- factor(cutree(cl_all$hc, k_all))
ph$km_ns  <- factor(kmeans(cl_ns$X, k_ns, nstart = 25)$cluster)
ph$hc_ns  <- factor(cutree(cl_ns$hc, k_ns))
c(k_all = k_all, ARI_all = round(ari(ph$km_all, ph$hc_all), 2),
  k_nosex = k_ns, ARI_nosex = round(ari(ph$km_ns, ph$hc_ns), 2))
table(kmeans_all = ph$km_all, sex = ph$sex)
table(kmeans_nosex = ph$km_ns, group = ph$group)
final_silhouette <- c(
  all = mean(silhouette(as.integer(ph$km_all), cl_all$d)[, 3]),
  nosex = mean(silhouette(as.integer(ph$km_ns), cl_ns$d)[, 3]))
final_silhouette
```

## Are clusters enriched for phenotypes?

Categorical phenotypes were tested with Fisher's exact test and continuous phenotypes with
the Kruskal-Wallis test; p-values were BH-adjusted within each clustering.

```{r enrich}
enrich <- function(cl) {
  cat_v <- c(sex = "sex", group = "group", diabetes = "diabetes")
  con_v <- c(age = "age", BMI = "bmi", HbA1c = "hba1c", SI = "si",
             fasting_insulin = "finsulin", fasting_glucose = "fglu")
  p <- c(sapply(cat_v, function(v) fisher.test(table(cl, ph[[v]]))$p.value),
         sapply(con_v, function(v) kruskal.test(ph[[v]] ~ cl)$p.value))
  data.frame(phenotype = names(p), p = signif(p, 2), q_BH = signif(p.adjust(p, "BH"), 2))
}
en <- merge(setNames(enrich(ph$km_all), c("phenotype", "p_all", "q_all")),
            setNames(enrich(ph$km_ns),  c("phenotype", "p_nosex", "q_nosex")))
knitr::kable(en[order(en$q_all), ], row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Phenotype enrichment of k-means clusters, all genes vs sex genes removed.")
write.csv(en, "results/cluster_enrichment.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r cluster-box, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="Phenotypes by k-means cluster (sex-associated genes removed)."}
long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("age", "bmi", "hba1c", "si"), function(v)
  data.frame(cluster = ph$km_ns, variable = v, value = ph[[v]])))
ggplot(long, aes(cluster, value, fill = cluster)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8) + facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**Do male and female patients form distinct clusters?** With all genes, the k-means partition
(k = `r k_all`) against sex has Fisher p = `r signif(en$p_all[en$phenotype=="sex"], 2)`.
After sex-associated genes are removed, that association becomes
p = `r signif(en$p_nosex[en$phenotype=="sex"], 2)`.

# Genes correlated with age

For every gene, the Pearson and Spearman correlation with age was computed across all 50
subjects, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Because the T2D group is older (H4), two robustness
checks were added: (a) a linear model `expression ~ age + sex + diabetes` fitted to every gene,
and (b) the correlation re-computed in the 40 non-diabetic subjects only.

```{r age-cor}
cor_test_vec <- function(M, x, method = "pearson") {
  use <- is.finite(x)
  M <- M[, use, drop = FALSE]; x <- x[use]
  stopifnot(ncol(M) > 2, all(is.finite(M)))
  r <- as.vector(cor(t(M), x, method = method))
  n <- length(x)
  tstat <- r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2))
  p <- 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), n - 2)
  data.frame(gene = rownames(M), r = r, p = p, q = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
}
# Classical OLS fitted by QR; returns a specified coefficient for every feature.
fit_feature_lm <- function(M, metadata, formula, term) {
  X <- model.matrix(formula, metadata)
  stopifnot(nrow(X) == ncol(M), all(is.finite(X)), all(is.finite(M)))
  fit <- lm.fit(X, t(M))
  stopifnot(fit$rank == ncol(X), nrow(X) > fit$rank)
  j <- match(term, colnames(X)); stopifnot(!is.na(j))
  unscaled <- chol2inv(qr.R(fit$qr))
  j_pivot <- match(j, fit$qr$pivot)
  residual_df <- nrow(X) - fit$rank
  s2 <- colSums(fit$residuals^2) / residual_df
  se <- sqrt(s2 * unscaled[j_pivot, j_pivot])
  beta <- as.vector(fit$coefficients[j, ])
  p <- 2 * pt(-abs(beta / se), residual_df)
  data.frame(gene = rownames(M), beta = beta, se = se,
             p = p, q = p.adjust(p, "BH"), row.names = NULL)
}
pear <- cor_test_vec(expr, ph$age, "pearson")
spear <- cor_test_vec(expr, ph$age, "spearman")
nd <- ph$diabetes == "No"
pear_nd <- cor_test_vec(expr[, nd], ph$age[nd], "pearson")
age_adjusted <- fit_feature_lm(expr, ph, ~ age + sex + diabetes, "age")
age_tab <- data.frame(gene = pear$gene, r_pearson = pear$r,
  p_pearson = pear$p, q_pearson = pear$q,
  r_spearman = spear$r, p_spearman = spear$p, q_spearman = spear$q,
  r_nondiabetic = pear_nd$r, p_nondiabetic = pear_nd$p,
  beta_age_adj = age_adjusted$beta, p_adj = age_adjusted$p,
  q_adj = age_adjusted$q)
age_tab <- age_tab[order(age_tab$p_pearson), ]
write.csv(age_tab, "results/age_correlation_all_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)
age_sig_counts <- c(
  pearson_q05 = sum(age_tab$q_pearson < 0.05),
  spearman_q05 = sum(age_tab$q_spearman < 0.05),
  adjusted_q05 = sum(age_tab$q_adj < 0.05),
  nondiabetic_p001 = sum(age_tab$p_nondiabetic < 0.001),
  pearson_p001 = sum(pear$p < 0.001))
age_sig_counts
```

```{r age-select}
# Age-gene set: Pearson FDR < 0.05; fall back to the top 100 by p if fewer than 30 pass
age_genes <- if (age_sig_counts["pearson_q05"] >= 30) age_tab$gene[age_tab$q_pearson < 0.05] else
  head(age_tab$gene, 100)
age_rule  <- if (age_sig_counts["pearson_q05"] >= 30) "Pearson FDR < 0.05" else "top 100 by Pearson p"
robust    <- age_tab$gene[age_tab$gene %in% age_genes & age_tab$q_adj < 0.1 &
                          sign(age_tab$r_nondiabetic) == sign(age_tab$r_pearson)]
c(n_age_genes = length(age_genes), n_up = sum(age_tab$r_pearson[age_tab$gene %in% age_genes] > 0),
  n_robust = length(robust))
knitr::kable(head(age_tab[, c("gene", "r_pearson", "q_pearson", "r_spearman",
                              "r_nondiabetic", "q_adj")], 20),
             digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Top 20 age-correlated genes. q_adj: FDR for age in expression ~ age + sex + diabetes.")
```

The age-ranked set (`r age_rule`) contains **`r length(age_genes)` expression features**.
It is an exploratory selection, not a list of 100 FDR-significant genes. Full-sample counts
at BH q < 0.05 are `r age_sig_counts["pearson_q05"]` (Pearson),
`r age_sig_counts["spearman_q05"]` (Spearman), and `r age_sig_counts["adjusted_q05"]`
(age adjusted for sex and diabetes). Spearman p-values use the asymptotic t approximation,
as in `cor.test(..., method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)`.
Within the selected set, `r length(robust)` feature meets the exploratory adjusted q < 0.1
rule and retains the Pearson direction in the overlapping non-diabetic subset. This is a
within-cohort consistency check, not independent replication. The age-ordered heatmap and
top-gene plots below visualize the selection and are not independent tests of it.

## Sensitivity of age associations to flagged samples

```{r age-sensitivity}
keep_s <- !(ph$sample %in% excl)
age_sensitivity <- fit_feature_lm(
  expr[, keep_s], ph[keep_s, ], ~ age + sex + diabetes, "age")
age_sensitivity <- age_sensitivity[order(age_sensitivity$p), ]
write.csv(age_sensitivity, "results/age_adjusted_sample_sensitivity.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
age_full_significant <- age_tab$gene[age_tab$q_adj < 0.05]
age_sens_significant <- age_sensitivity$gene[age_sensitivity$q < 0.05]
comparison_genes <- unique(c(age_full_significant, age_sens_significant))
age_sample_comparison <- data.frame(
  gene = comparison_genes,
  beta_all = age_tab$beta_age_adj[match(comparison_genes, age_tab$gene)],
  q_all = age_tab$q_adj[match(comparison_genes, age_tab$gene)],
  beta_without_flags = age_sensitivity$beta[
    match(comparison_genes, age_sensitivity$gene)],
  q_without_flags = age_sensitivity$q[
    match(comparison_genes, age_sensitivity$gene)])
knitr::kable(age_sample_comparison, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Same age + sex + diabetes model and feature universe: all 50 vs 46 samples.")
write.csv(age_sample_comparison, "results/age_sample_comparison.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

After excluding `r paste(ph$label[!keep_s], collapse = ", ")`, the identical adjusted model
and BH correction across all `r nrow(expr)` features identify
**`r paste(age_sens_significant, collapse = ", ")`** at q < 0.05
(`r paste(fmt_q(age_sensitivity$q[match(age_sens_significant, age_sensitivity$gene)]), collapse = ", ")`).
The full-sample significant feature is **`r paste(age_full_significant, collapse = ", ")`**.
For UNC13C, adjusted q changes from
`r fmt_q(age_tab$q_adj[match("UNC13C", age_tab$gene)])` to
`r fmt_q(age_sensitivity$q[match("UNC13C", age_sensitivity$gene)])`.
Thus the identity of the 5%-FDR age signal changes from
`r paste(age_full_significant, collapse = ", ")` to
`r paste(age_sens_significant, collapse = ", ")` when these samples are excluded. UNC13C still meets the exploratory 10% threshold after exclusion, but not 5%.
This dependence on sample selection limits a claim of a stable age-gene signature; it does
not prove that the flagged samples should be removed.

# Principal component analysis

PCA (`prcomp`) was run on all `r nrow(expr)` expression features, each centered to mean zero but not scaled
(the data are already on a log scale, so unscaled PCA keeps high-variance genes influential).
It was repeated after removing sex-associated genes. Each point is labeled with the subject
code (N = FH-, P = FH+, D = T2D, followed by the GEO sample number within the group).

```{r pca}
pca    <- prcomp(t(expr), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
pca_ns <- prcomp(t(expr_ns), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
ve     <- 100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
ve_ns  <- 100 * pca_ns$sdev^2 / sum(pca_ns$sdev^2)
round(rbind(all = ve[1:6], no_sex = ve_ns[1:6]), 1)
pcd <- cbind(ph, pca$x[, 1:6]); pcd_ns <- cbind(ph, pca_ns$x[, 1:6])
```

```{r pca-sex, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="PCA of all genes, colored by sex, shaped by group."}
ggplot(pcd, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = sex, shape = group)) + geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.4, max.overlaps = 50, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ann_col$Sex) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve[2]))
```

```{r pca-age, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="PCA after removing sex-associated genes, colored by age, shaped by group."}
ggplot(pcd_ns, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = age, shape = group)) + geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.4, max.overlaps = 50, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve_ns[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve_ns[2]))
```

**Matched PCA sensitivity analysis.** To isolate the effect of sample inclusion, the next
two PCAs use the same 1,000 non-sex features selected in the full dataset and the same
centering/unit-variance scaling rule. One includes all 50 samples, the other excludes the
four exploratory flags. This pair separates sample inclusion from the different feature
selection/scaling choices used by the preceding all-feature PCAs. PC axes are estimated
anew in each fit; PC2 should not be assumed to represent an identical biological axis.

```{r pca-matched-full, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Matched PCA control: all 50 samples, fixed top 1,000 non-sex features, scaled. Compare with the next panel."}
pca_matched <- prcomp(t(expr_ns[top_ns, ]), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
ve_matched <- 100 * pca_matched$sdev^2 / sum(pca_matched$sdev^2)
pcd_matched <- cbind(ph, pca_matched$x[, 1:6])
ggplot(pcd_matched, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group, size = bmi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.4, max.overlaps = 50,
                  show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ann_col$Group) + scale_size(range = c(1.2, 4)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve_matched[1]),
       y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve_matched[2]))
```

```{r pca-sens, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Matched PCA sensitivity: 46 samples after excluding exploratory QC flags; same top 1,000 non-sex features and scaling rule. Color: group; size: BMI."}
keep_s  <- !(ph$sample %in% excl)
pca_s   <- prcomp(t(expr_ns[top_ns, keep_s]), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
ve_s    <- 100 * pca_s$sdev^2 / sum(pca_s$sdev^2)
pcd_s   <- cbind(ph[keep_s, ], pca_s$x[, 1:6])
ggplot(pcd_s, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group, size = bmi)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.4, max.overlaps = 50, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ann_col$Group) + scale_size(range = c(1.2, 4)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve_s[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve_s[2]))
```

```{r pc-assoc}
pc_assoc <- function(d, analysis) {
  vars <- c("age", "bmi", "hba1c", "si", "finsulin")
  do.call(rbind, lapply(paste0("PC", 1:6), function(pc) {
    p <- c(sex = wilcox.test(d[[pc]] ~ d$sex)$p.value,
      group = kruskal.test(d[[pc]] ~ d$group)$p.value,
      sapply(vars, function(v)
        cor.test(d[[pc]], d[[v]], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value))
    n <- c(sex = sum(complete.cases(d[, c(pc, "sex")])),
      group = sum(complete.cases(d[, c(pc, "group")])),
      sapply(vars, function(v) sum(complete.cases(d[, c(pc, v)]))))
    data.frame(analysis = analysis, PC = pc, phenotype = names(p),
               n = as.integer(n), p = as.numeric(p))
  }))
}
pc_associations <- rbind(pc_assoc(pcd, "all_features"),
  pc_assoc(pcd_ns, "nonsex_features"),
  pc_assoc(pcd_matched, "matched_50"), pc_assoc(pcd_s, "matched_46"))
# Each of the four declared analyses has 6 PCs x 7 phenotypes = 42 tests.
pc_associations$q_within <- ave(pc_associations$p, pc_associations$analysis,
                               FUN = function(p) p.adjust(p, "BH"))
pc_associations$q_all <- p.adjust(pc_associations$p, "BH")
write.csv(pc_associations, "results/pc_phenotype_associations.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
pc_nominal <- pc_associations[pc_associations$p < 0.05, ]
knitr::kable(pc_nominal, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Nominal p < 0.05 rows shown after BH correction of all 42 tests per PCA and all 168 tests together. Full results are exported.")
pc2_sensitivity <- pc_associations[
  pc_associations$analysis == "matched_46" & pc_associations$PC == "PC2", ]
```

There are `r nrow(pc_associations)` PC--phenotype tests in total. Within-PCA BH q < 0.05
is reached by `r sum(pc_associations$q_within < 0.05)` tests; across-all-analyses BH q < 0.05
by `r sum(pc_associations$q_all < 0.05)`. In the 46-sample PCA, the PC2--SI association has
p = `r fmt_q(pc2_sensitivity$p[pc2_sensitivity$phenotype == "si"])` and
within-PCA q = `r fmt_q(pc2_sensitivity$q_within[pc2_sensitivity$phenotype == "si"])`.
It is a nominal exploratory association, not an FDR-significant finding.

```{r pc-loadings}
ld <- pca_ns$rotation
data.frame(PC1_top_pos = names(head(sort(ld[, 1], decreasing = TRUE), 10)),
           PC1_top_neg = names(head(sort(ld[, 1]), 10)),
           PC2_top_pos = names(head(sort(ld[, 2], decreasing = TRUE), 10)),
           PC2_top_neg = names(head(sort(ld[, 2]), 10)))
```

# Additional analysis: insulin sensitivity and diabetes

As an exploratory extension, every gene was correlated (Spearman) with insulin sensitivity
(SI, n = 48), and T2D was compared with FH- subjects (Welch t-test). Genes from Jin et al.'s
SRF story (SRF, its co-activator MKL1/MRTF-A, and the SRF targets ACTA2, FHL1, VCL, CNN2) are
checked individually. These targeted checks reuse the original study's public cohort;
they are not independent replication. The Welch contrast is unadjusted; an additional
model below estimates the T2D--FH- difference conditional on age and reported sex.

```{r si}
si_ok <- !is.na(ph$si)
si_cor <- cor_test_vec(expr[, si_ok], ph$si[si_ok], "spearman")
si_cor <- si_cor[order(si_cor$p), ]
c(si_q05 = sum(si_cor$q < 0.05), si_p001 = sum(si_cor$p < 0.001))
write.csv(si_cor, "results/si_correlation_all_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

d_vs_n <- ph$group %in% c("T2D", "FH-")
grp <- droplevels(ph$group[d_vs_n])
de_p <- apply(expr[, d_vs_n], 1, function(g) t.test(g ~ grp)$p.value)
de_fc <- rowMeans(expr[, ph$group == "T2D"]) - rowMeans(expr[, ph$group == "FH-"])
de <- data.frame(gene = names(de_p), log_diff_T2D_vs_FHneg = de_fc, p = de_p,
                 q = p.adjust(de_p, "BH"))[order(de_p), ]
c(de_q05 = sum(de$q < 0.05), de_p001 = sum(de$p < 0.001))
write.csv(de, "results/T2D_vs_FHneg.csv", row.names = FALSE)
de_adjusted <- fit_feature_lm(expr, ph, ~ age + sex + group, "groupT2D")
de_adjusted <- de_adjusted[order(de_adjusted$p), ]
write.csv(de_adjusted, "results/T2D_vs_FHneg_age_sex_adjusted.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

srf <- intersect(c("SRF", "MKL1", "MRTFA", "ACTA2", "FHL1", "VCL", "CNN2", "MYH11"), rownames(expr))
knitr::kable(data.frame(gene = srf,
  r_SI = si_cor$r[match(srf, si_cor$gene)], p_SI = si_cor$p[match(srf, si_cor$gene)],
  diff_T2D_FHneg = de$log_diff_T2D_vs_FHneg[match(srf, de$gene)],
  p_T2D_FHneg = de$p[match(srf, de$gene)]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Selected SRF-related genes: unadjusted associations and nominal p-values; these are not measurements of SRF transcriptional activity.")
c(overlap_age_SI = length(intersect(age_genes, head(si_cor$gene, length(age_genes)))))
```

```{r volcano, fig.height=4, fig.cap="T2D vs FH-: difference in mean log expression vs significance."}
de$lab <- ifelse(rank(de$p) <= 15, de$gene, "")
ggplot(de, aes(log_diff_T2D_vs_FHneg, -log10(p))) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(data = de[de$lab != "", ], colour = "#D95F02", size = 1.2) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 30) +
  labs(x = "mean log expression, T2D minus FH-", y = "-log10 p")
```

The unadjusted Welch comparison yields `r sum(de$q < 0.05)` features at BH q < 0.05;
the age/sex-adjusted T2D contrast yields `r sum(de_adjusted$q < 0.05)`.
The latter includes all three groups in `expression ~ age + sex + group`, with FH- as
reference. BMI is not included in this primary descriptive contrast: whether to adjust
for adiposity depends on the intended estimand. Neither contrast identifies a causal
diabetes effect, and residual confounding remains possible.

# DAVID functional enrichment (Part III)

Five gene lists are written to `results/` and analyzed with the DAVID Functional Annotation
Chart (<https://davidbioinformatics.nih.gov>, run on October 21, 2026; the site listed
Knowledgebase v2026_2 as its latest release): genes decreasing with age (`age_down`), genes
increasing with age (`age_up`), the top 100 marker genes of each k-means cluster after sex-gene
removal (`cluster1_up`, `cluster2_up`), and the 200 genes most correlated with insulin
sensitivity (`SI_top200`). The single robust age gene was not submitted. Settings: identifier
OFFICIAL_GENE_SYMBOL, species *Homo sapiens*, background = DAVID's built-in *Human Genome U133
Plus 2 Array* population (the array used here, so the background is the genes measurable on
this platform), categories KEGG_PATHWAY and GOTERM_BP_DIRECT, default chart thresholds
(Count >= 2, EASE p <= 0.1). Probe sets annotated with several symbols (`A///B`) were split
into separate symbols before upload. DAVID is a web tool, so its output is stored unchanged in
`data/david/` and read back here. DAVID's `Benjamini` column is the ordinary BH
adjustment; its `FDR` column is the adaptive linear step-up adjustment described by
Benjamini and Hochberg (2000). The reported enrichment threshold uses the latter.
The platform background is appropriate to the supplied metadata; a separately justified
analysis could instead use the actual tested/mappable universe. Multi-symbol features
remain ambiguous measurements even after splitting symbols for annotation.

**Cache validity:** this document does not query DAVID automatically. Frozen normalized
input lists are stored with the imported tables. A render must stop if the newly generated
lists differ; changing a threshold, clustering result, or gene selection then requires a
new DAVID run and a coordinated update of the frozen lists and results.

```{r export}
up   <- age_tab$gene[age_tab$gene %in% age_genes & age_tab$r_pearson > 0]
down <- age_tab$gene[age_tab$gene %in% age_genes & age_tab$r_pearson < 0]
writeLines(up,   "results/DAVID_age_up.txt")
writeLines(down, "results/DAVID_age_down.txt")
writeLines(robust, "results/DAVID_age_robust.txt")
writeLines(head(si_cor$gene, 200), "results/DAVID_SI_top200.txt")
writeLines(rownames(expr), "results/DAVID_background.txt")
# cluster marker genes: top 100 genes by t-statistic for each no-sex k-means cluster
for (k in levels(ph$km_ns)) {
  tk <- apply(expr_ns, 1, function(g) t.test(g[ph$km_ns == k], g[ph$km_ns != k])$statistic)
  writeLines(names(head(sort(tk, decreasing = TRUE), 100)),
             sprintf("results/DAVID_cluster%s_up.txt", k))
}
c(age_up = length(up), age_down = length(down), robust = length(robust))
```

```{r david}
normalize_david_symbols <- function(x) {
  y <- toupper(trimws(unlist(strsplit(x, "///", fixed = TRUE))))
  unique(y[nzchar(y)])
}
check_david_inputs <- function(current, frozen) {
  if (!setequal(names(current), names(frozen)))
    stop("DAVID list names changed; rerun DAVID and update its frozen inputs/results.")
  changed <- names(current)[!vapply(names(current), function(n)
    setequal(current[[n]], frozen[[n]]), logical(1))]
  if (length(changed)) stop("Stale DAVID results for: ", paste(changed, collapse = ", "),
    ". Rerun DAVID and update its frozen inputs/results before rendering.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}
david_list_names <- c("age_down", "age_up",
  paste0("cluster", levels(ph$km_ns), "_up"), "SI_top200")
david_current_symbols <- setNames(lapply(david_list_names, function(n)
  normalize_david_symbols(readLines(paste0("results/DAVID_", n, ".txt")))),
  david_list_names)
david_frozen_names <- read.delim("data/david/DAVID_run_info.tsv")$List
david_frozen_symbols <- setNames(lapply(david_frozen_names, function(n)
  readLines(paste0("data/david/input_symbols/", n, ".txt"))), david_frozen_names)
check_david_inputs(david_current_symbols, david_frozen_symbols)
dv <- read.delim("data/david/DAVID_chart_results.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
dinfo <- read.delim("data/david/DAVID_run_info.tsv")
lists <- dinfo$List
dv$Category <- ifelse(dv$Category == "KEGG_PATHWAY", "KEGG", "GO-BP")
dv$Term <- sub("^(hsa[0-9]+:|GO:[0-9]+~)", "", dv$Term)
dinfo$terms_p_le_0.1 <- as.vector(table(factor(dv$List, lists)))
dinfo$terms_FDR_lt_0.05 <- as.vector(table(factor(dv$List[dv$FDR < 0.05], lists)))
knitr::kable(dinfo[, c("List", "input_symbols", "DAVID_IDs", "terms_p_le_0.1", "terms_FDR_lt_0.05")],
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "DAVID input lists: symbols submitted, symbols mapped to DAVID IDs, and KEGG + GO-BP terms returned.")
top <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(dv, list(dv$List, dv$Category), drop = TRUE),
                             function(d) head(d[order(d$PValue), ], 3)))
top <- top[order(match(top$List, lists), top$Category != "KEGG", top$PValue), ]
top$Term <- ifelse(nchar(top$Term) > 48, paste0(substr(top$Term, 1, 45), "..."), top$Term)
top$fold <- round(top$`Fold Enrichment`, 1)
top$p <- signif(top$PValue, 2); top$FDR <- signif(top$FDR, 2)
knitr::kable(top[, c("List", "Category", "Term", "Count", "fold", "p", "FDR")], row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Top 3 KEGG and top 3 GO-BP terms per list (DAVID EASE p; FDR < 0.05 only in age_down).")
david_sig_terms <- dv[dv$FDR < 0.05,
  c("List", "Category", "Term", "Count", "Genes", "FDR")]
david_sig_terms$FDR <- signif(david_sig_terms$FDR, 2)
knitr::kable(david_sig_terms[, setdiff(names(david_sig_terms), "List")],
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "All DAVID terms with FDR < 0.05 (age_down list) and the genes that drive them.")
```

Both the ordinary BH and adaptive-FDR columns identify `r nrow(david_sig_terms)` terms
below 0.05 in this saved result; all are in the age-down list. This agreement does not make
the two correction methods identical.

**Interpretation.** Only the age-decreasing list gives terms that survive adaptive FDR < 0.05,
and several overlapping terms describe mitochondrial energy metabolism. KEGG carbon metabolism, lipoic acid
metabolism and the citrate (TCA) cycle, and GO-BP tricarboxylic acid cycle, malate-aspartate
shuttle and mitochondrial fission are all enriched, driven by a small core of genes (DLAT and
PDHB of pyruvate dehydrogenase, MDH2, GOT1, GCSH, L2HGDH, SLC25A12, and the fission genes MFF,
MUL1 and MTFR1L). This is an exploratory functional theme relevant to the mitochondrial
hallmark of aging; expression-based over-representation does not demonstrate mitochondrial
dysfunction or an age-specific mechanism. Extracellular-matrix and inflammation terms are
not significant in these selected lists, which does not establish absence of those processes. The genes increasing with age show only a nominal mRNA-splicing
signal (FDR about 0.96). The two cluster marker lists give only nominal terms (cluster 1:
growth-factor receptor signaling through PDGFRB, FGFR2 and VEGFA; cluster 2: Polycomb
repressive complex, splicing and endocytosis, best FDR = 0.09). These are exploratory
descriptions of expression-defined clusters, not independent validation of the clusters. The SI list has no pathway-level signal, so the SRF result
above rests on the targeted gene tests, not on DAVID.

# Discussion

**Unsupervised structure and H1.** Under the chosen feature selection, scaling, distance,
and clustering methods, separation is weak: final silhouette widths are
`r paste(round(final_silhouette, 3), collapse = " and ")`, and k-means/hierarchical ARI is
`r round(ari(ph$km_all, ph$hc_all), 2)`. Selecting the best k among 2--6 does not prove
that discrete biological subgroups exist. Cluster enrichment for SI is nominal
(p = `r en$p_all[en$phenotype == "SI"]`, q = `r en$q_all[en$phenotype == "SI"]`);
no tested phenotype survives within-clustering BH q < 0.05. H1 is not clearly supported.
The SI/BMI/insulin trends are hypotheses for follow-up, not established drivers of the
partition. Cluster-marker rankings use the same expression data that defined the clusters,
so they describe those clusters rather than independently validate them.

**Sex and H2.** The `r length(sex_genes)` features meeting the chosen sex-effect thresholds
account for `r round(100 * sex_variance_fraction, 2)`% of the sum of feature variances.
Removing them changes the global results modestly, and the selected clusters do not show
an FDR-significant sex association. H2 is not supported by this analysis. This is not
evidence that sex has no expression effects or that a small number of genes cannot dominate
another dataset; the variance contribution and the actual PCA/clustering results matter.

**QC and PCA interpretation.** N1 and P25 are sex-marker discrepancy flags; P1 and D10 are
lower-correlation flags. Their causes remain unverified. Main analyses retain all samples
and their recorded labels. Correlation 0.874 is a dataset-specific diagnostic, not evidence
that the arrays are noisier than RNA-seq. Loadings may suggest tissue composition or sample
quality hypotheses, but these explanations have not been established by independent QC.
The matched 50/46-sample PCA pair fixes the feature selection and scaling rule. The nominal
PC2--SI association after exclusions has within-PCA q =
`r fmt_q(pc2_sensitivity$q_within[pc2_sensitivity$phenotype == "si"])`;
it should not be promoted to a significant result after screening multiple PCs/phenotypes.

**Age associations, H3, and H4.** Pearson testing yields no 5%-FDR features, but this does
not describe all age analyses: UNC13C has Spearman q =
`r fmt_q(age_tab$q_spearman[match("UNC13C", age_tab$gene)])` and adjusted-model q =
`r fmt_q(age_tab$q_adj[match("UNC13C", age_tab$gene)])` in the full sample. With the four
flags excluded, PLAG1 becomes the only adjusted-model feature below 5% FDR
(q = `r fmt_q(age_sensitivity$q[match("PLAG1", age_sensitivity$gene)])`), while UNC13C
rises to q = `r fmt_q(age_sensitivity$q[match("UNC13C", age_sensitivity$gene)])`.
The identity of the significant feature is therefore sensitive to sample inclusion.
The top-100 Pearson list remains explicitly exploratory. Its age-decreasing features are
enriched for several overlapping mitochondrial/metabolic terms, a functional theme
consistent with part of H3, but not proof of impaired function or causal aging mechanisms.
The T2D group is older and the adjusted/subgroup analyses alter the evidence, supporting
concern about confounding in H4. They do not determine how much of the association is
caused by age, diabetes, adiposity, or other correlated factors. The non-diabetic subset
overlaps the full cohort and is not independent replication.

**Relationship to Jin et al.** SRF and MKL1 expression have nominal negative associations
with SI in this dataset. Some selected target genes also have nominal unadjusted T2D--FH-
differences. These checks reuse the original cohort and do not reproduce the paper's
SRF-target gene-set analysis or its animal/cell perturbations. SRF/MKL1 mRNA abundance
does not directly measure SRF transcriptional activity. The appropriate claim is partial
consistency of expression directions, not independent replication or a verified mechanism.
The unadjusted disease comparison is susceptible to age/sex/adiposity confounding;
the additional age/sex-adjusted contrast is descriptive and does not remove all such risks.

**Limitations and unsuccessful approaches.** Weak cluster separation, no Pearson-FDR age
features, and sensitivity of the adjusted age signal are substantive results, not reasons
to relax a confirmatory threshold. The rank-based top-100 list is a separately labeled
exploratory analysis. Small groups, a cross-sectional age range of 21--67 years,
age--diabetes imbalance, missing clinical measures, ambiguous gene annotations, and
unverified QC flags limit interpretation. No causal effects or general aging biomarker
claims are established. A stronger follow-up could use explicitly justified covariates,
moderated microarray models such as limma, ranked gene-set tests, and independent data.
